$comment: Spec R7: the renames the source itself does not record. Measured 2026-11-12 on the live wiki: there is no champion redirect table (the export endpoint answers `Table ChampionRedirects not found`), `Champions.KeyDdragon` is empty for every champion, and `ScoreboardPlayers` stores the *current* champion name in every era — a 2011-06-18 row and a 2012-11-29 row both already say `Nunu & Willump`. A retired champion name therefore cannot resolve from the source alone, and a payload that cited `Nunu` would mint a second champion entity, which is exactly the duplicate a rename must not create (spec D3). An entry here is a reviewed statement about one string. Its target is normally a page (team/player) or Riot's numeric id (champion), never a display name, because the display name is the thing that changes. The exception is `aliasOf`: when the corpus carries no registry row for the entity at all — every team in IPL 5 2012 is in that state, because that crawl fetched games, players, series and drafts, not `Teams` — there is no page or id to point at, and the entry instead states that one observed source string denotes the same entity as another observed source string. `aliasOf` resolves through the registries first, mints the target string's provisional id otherwise, and refuses to chain onto another declaration. `reason` is mandatory for the same reason the event rule's overrides require one: this file is human judgement, so it has to state the judgement.
description: Source strings that denote an existing entity but that no registry payload in the source records, each with its stated reason.

aliases.reason: Riot renamed the champion Nunu to Nunu & Willump in its 2019 rework; the champion id (20) did not change, and the source's own ReleaseDate for that id (2009-02-21) is when the old name started applying. The wiki carries only the new name in every era it covers, so the old string has no observed use in this corpus: `from` is the measured release date and `until` stays null rather than asserting a rename date the source does not record.

IPL 5 2012 (the earliest event with games) has the two source tables disagreeing about this team's name and nothing else: the 6 `MatchSchedule` rows that name this roster in its 2012 form say `CLG Prime`, while the 12 games in those series and every `ScoreboardPlayers` row say `Counter Logic Gaming`. The same event's three wildcard-qualifier series (2012-11-16 to 2012-11-17) already use `Counter Logic Gaming`, so the org name is the one the source uses earliest; the `CLG Prime` series run from 2012-11-29 to 2012-12-02. That is one roster under the name it was playing as, not two teams: the two strings never appear on opposite sides of a game and never meet in one, and the teams that bracket the six `CLG Prime` series (Team FeaR, Counter Logic Gaming Europe, Fnatic, Moscow Five, Team Curse Europe) oppose the same roster in those games, which spell `Counter Logic Gaming`. CLG Prime is the 2012-era name the wiki gave the main Counter Logic Gaming roster, and it is also how `MatchSchedule` still stores it; the games store the org name. No `Teams` or `TeamRedirects` payload for this event is committed, so the corpus records neither string as a page: the declaration therefore states `aliasOf` rather than a `page` target, and the source strings stay on both rows (spec R7) while the canonical id is the one `Counter Logic Gaming` would mint on its own. `from` is the first date the declared string `CLG Prime` is used in the recorded corpus: 2012-10-04, when the full crawl (ticket 16) brought Worlds Season 2 in and its group-stage series name this roster `CLG Prime` as well. The window moved from 2012-11-29 when that crawl landed, because a declared window bounds every lookup and the string is used earlier than the ten-event corpus could show (ticket 15). It is not the first date either string is used, because the alias table dates `Counter Logic Gaming` from the wildcard qualifiers on 2012-11-16. `until` stays null because the source records no rename date.
